library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Emoto_2016_sirolimus"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12096>
* PMCID: PMC4999604

Emoto 2016 used sirolimus whole-blood troughs from a
concentration-controlled phase II trial in children with complicated
vascular anomalies (NCT00975819) to describe how sirolimus clearance
develops over the first years of life. The paper contributes three
models, all packaged here and all described in this one article:

* **`Emoto_2016_sirolimus`** -- the paper's population model (Table 2).
  Maximum a posteriori Bayesian clearance estimates, one per sample,
  were normalised to 70 kg with a weight exponent of 0.67 and fitted
  in NONMEM 7.2 (FOCE-I, `$PRED`) as a sigmoid Emax function of
  postmenstrual age (PMA), with exponential IIV on all three parameters
  and a proportional residual error.
* **`Emoto_2016_sirolimus_25oh_ratio`** and
  **`Emoto_2016_sirolimus_16odm_ratio`** -- simple Emax regressions
  (GraphPad Prism) of the 25-hydroxysirolimus and
  16-O-demethylsirolimus to sirolimus concentration ratios on PMA
  (Figure 3A and 3B), the CYP3A-activity markers the authors used to
  explain the clearance maturation.

None of the three is a concentration-time model. The observation of
the first is a clearance (L/h/70kg) and of the other two a
dimensionless metabolite / parent ratio, each a function of a PMA
covariate. There are no doses, volumes or absorption parameters,
because the Bayesian estimator only estimated individual clearances
from the predominantly trough samples (Methods, "Individual clearance
estimates by Bayesian estimation"). For that reason the PKNCA section
of the usual validation template does not apply; the checks below are
instead against the paper's printed estimates, Figure 1, the Figure 2
visual predictive check and Figure 3.

# Population

The trial enrolled 52 patients aged 21 days to 19 years (Table 1;
median weight 18 kg, range 4.0-101; 20 male, 32 female; 39 Caucasian,
7 African American, 1 Asian, 4 other, 1 unknown). Oral sirolimus
started at 0.8 mg/m^2 twice daily and was then titrated to a trough of
10-15 ng/mL. Patients had adequate liver and renal function and no
CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers at entry; seven patients with
kaposiform hemangioendothelioma received tapering steroids for 1-2
months, which had no significant covariate effect.

Two subsets were analysed:

* The **maturation fit** used all 316 serial clearance estimates from
  the 24 patients younger than 4 years (Supplemental Table 2: PMA
  43-233 weeks, median 120; weight 4.0-18 kg, median 11; 10 male, 14
  female). The cohort had no premature infants, so PMA was computed as
  postnatal age + 40 weeks.
* The **weight exponent** came from a separate log-log regression of
  each patient's averaged first-three-month clearance on body weight in
  the 32 patients aged 3-19 years (Supplemental Table 1 and
  Supplemental Figure 1A: slope 0.67, 95% CI 0.47-0.88), on the
  assumption that maturation is complete by age 3.

The metabolite-ratio regressions used the samples from patients
younger than 4 years plotted in Figure 3 (about 29 and 28 points); the
number of contributing patients is not reported.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Sigmoid Emax `CL = CLmatured * PMA^Hill / (TM50^Hill + PMA^Hill)` | -- | Methods, "Population modeling analysis"; Supplement 2 (`$PRED`) |
| PMA = postnatal age (weeks) + 40 | -- | Methods, "Population modeling analysis" |
| Size normalisation `CL70 = CLobs * (70 / WT)^0.67` | -- | Results equation; Supplemental Figure 1 legend |
| `lcl` (CLmatured) | 18.1 L/h/70kg | Table 2 (RSE 4.7%); Results; Figure 1 legend |
| `ltm50_cl` (TM50) | 62.9 weeks | Table 2 (RSE 8.4%) |
| `lhill` (Hill) | 2.94 | Table 2 (RSE 16.4%) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.67, fixed | Results; Supplemental Figure 1A |
| IIV form `P_i = P_pop * exp(eta_i)` | -- | Supplement 1, eq. 1; Supplement 2 |
| `etalcl`, `etaltm50_cl`, `etalhill` | 11.3, 17.4, 102 CV% | Table 2, IIV column |
| Residual `Y = F * (1 + eps)` | -- | Supplement 1, eq. 2; Supplement 2 |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.066) | Table 2 "Proportional residual error" 0.066 (variance) |
| Ratio model `ratio = Emax * PMA / (EC50 + PMA)` | -- | Methods, "Statistical analyses"; Figure 3 |
| 25-OH ratio `lemax`, `ltm50`, `addSd` | 0.184, 129 weeks, 0.029 | digitised from Figure 3A |
| 16-O-DM ratio `lemax`, `ltm50`, `addSd` | 0.136, 153 weeks, 0.023 | digitised from Figure 3B |

# Validation 1: the typical maturation curve (Figure 1)

The clearance model is algebraic in the `PAGE` covariate. The rxode2
time axis is not used by the model, so it is set equal to PMA in weeks
purely to give each row a distinct time.

```{r typical-sim}
cl_mod <- readModelDb("Emoto_2016_sirolimus")
cl_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(cl_mod)

pma_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(40, 260, by = 1), 62.9, 144, 196)))
grid_data <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = pma_grid, evid = 0L, PAGE = pma_grid, WT = 11
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(cl_typ, grid_data, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()

at_pma <- function(p) {
  v <- typ$CL_wt70[match(p, typ$PAGE)]
  if (anyNA(v)) stop("PMA value(s) not on the simulation grid")
  v
}
```

```{r typical-checks}
clmat <- 18.1; tm50 <- 62.9; hill <- 2.94
hand <- function(p) clmat * p^hill / (tm50^hill + p^hill)
typ_checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Check = c(
    "CL at PMA = TM50 equals CLmatured / 2",
    "Solved curve equals the Methods equation at every grid point",
    "Fraction of CLmatured at PMA 144 weeks (about 2 years)",
    "Fraction of CLmatured at PMA 196 weeks (about 3 years)",
    "CL at PMA 600 weeks vs the older-patient centred value 18.2 L/h/70kg"
  ),
  Expected = c(clmat / 2, 0, NA, NA, 18.2),
  Achieved = c(
    at_pma(tm50),
    max(abs(typ$CL_wt70 - hand(typ$PAGE))),
    at_pma(144) / clmat,
    at_pma(196) / clmat,
    hand(600)
  )
)
knitr::kable(typ_checks, digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic algebra: exact identities.
  abs(at_pma(tm50) - clmat / 2) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(typ$CL_wt70 - hand(typ$PAGE))) < 1e-8,
  all(diff(typ$CL_wt70) > 0),
  # Discussion: clearance "reached what was considered the mature level
  # ... at around 2-3 years of age (PMA of 144-196 weeks)".
  at_pma(144) / clmat > 0.90,
  at_pma(196) / clmat > 0.95,
  # Discussion: CLmatured agrees with the centred size-normalised clearance
  # of the 3-19 year olds (18.2 L/h/70kg, Supplemental Figure 1B).
  abs(hand(600) / 18.2 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The individual clearance in L/h is recovered from the size-normalised
prediction with the same 0.67 exponent the authors used to normalise
it. For a typical infant at PMA 100 weeks weighing 10 kg:

```{r absolute-cl}
one <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 100, evid = 0L, PAGE = 100, WT = 10)
one_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(cl_typ, one))
stopifnot(abs(one_sim$CL_abs - hand(100) * (10 / 70)^0.67) < 1e-8)
knitr::kable(
  one_sim |>
    dplyr::select(CL_wt70, CL_abs) |>
    dplyr::rename("CL (L/h/70kg)" = CL_wt70, "CL (L/h), 10 kg" = CL_abs),
  digits = 3
)
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Emoto 2016: typical size-normalised sirolimus clearance against postmenstrual age (CLmatured 18.1 L/h/70kg, TM50 62.9 weeks, Hill 2.94). The dashed line is CLmatured; the dotted line marks TM50."}
ggplot2::ggplot(typ, ggplot2::aes(PAGE, CL_wt70)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = clmat, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = tm50, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 35)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)",
                y = "Allometrically normalised CL (L/h/70kg)") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

# Validation 2: the visual predictive check (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the model's
simulated clearances. The maintainers digitised the black (simulated)
percentile lines from the published figure at four PMA values; they
are approximate (read from a 270-pixel image) and are used here only
to adjudicate the residual-error scale, which Table 2 prints as a bare
"0.066".

```{r vpc-sim}
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~PAGE, ~p05,  ~p50,  ~p95,
     82,   NA,  10.4,  19.5,
    131,  7.5,    NA,  24.1,
    200,  8.6,  16.1,  25.5,
    227,  8.7,  16.4,  25.8
)

n_sub <- 200
vpc_pma <- c(fig2$PAGE, seq(45, 245, by = 10))
vpc_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), PAGE = sort(unique(vpc_pma))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = PAGE, evid = 0L, WT = 11)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160801)
sim_var <- rxode2::rxSolve(cl_mod, vpc_data, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()

# Alternative reading: 0.066 as a standard deviation rather than a variance.
cl_mod_sd <- cl_mod |> rxode2::ini(propSd = 0.066)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160801)
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(cl_mod_sd, vpc_data, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()

pct <- function(d) {
  d |>
    dplyr::group_by(PAGE) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p05 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = stats::median(sim),
      p95 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
    )
}
q_var <- pct(sim_var)
q_sd <- pct(sim_sd)
```

```{r vpc-table}
cmp <- fig2 |>
  dplyr::left_join(q_var, by = "PAGE", suffix = c("_fig", "_var")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(q_sd |> dplyr::rename(p05_sd = p05, p50_sd = p50, p95_sd = p95),
                   by = "PAGE")
knitr::kable(
  cmp |>
    dplyr::select(PAGE, p05_fig, p05_var, p05_sd, p50_fig, p50_var, p50_sd,
                  p95_fig, p95_var, p95_sd) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "PMA (weeks)" = PAGE,
      "5th, Fig 2" = p05_fig, "5th, sigma variance" = p05_var, "5th, sigma SD" = p05_sd,
      "50th, Fig 2" = p50_fig, "50th, sigma variance" = p50_var, "50th, sigma SD" = p50_sd,
      "95th, Fig 2" = p95_fig, "95th, sigma variance" = p95_var, "95th, sigma SD" = p95_sd
    ),
  digits = 1
)
```

Reading 0.066 as the NONMEM `$SIGMA` variance (proportional SD 25.7%)
reproduces the published prediction interval; reading it as an SD
(6.6%) gives an interval roughly half as wide. The gate below uses
the width of the 90% interval in the mature region (PMA 200-227 weeks,
400 simulated values per percentile) as a ratio, which is robust to
which simulated subjects land in the tails; the table shows the value
read from the figure next to the two readings.

```{r vpc-gate}
mature <- function(d) {
  x <- d$sim[d$PAGE %in% c(200, 227)]
  unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.95) / stats::quantile(x, 0.05))
}
fig_ratio <- mean(c(25.5 / 8.6, 25.8 / 8.7))
ratio_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Source = c("Figure 2", "propSd = sqrt(0.066) (packaged)", "propSd = 0.066"),
  `95th / 5th percentile, PMA 200-227` = c(fig_ratio, mature(sim_var), mature(sim_sd))
)
knitr::kable(ratio_tab, digits = 2)
med_mature <- stats::median(sim_var$sim[sim_var$PAGE %in% c(200, 227)])
stopifnot(
  abs(mature(sim_var) / fig_ratio - 1) < 0.20,
  mature(sim_sd) < 2.3,
  abs(med_mature / 16.25 - 1) < 0.10
)
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Emoto 2016: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of size-normalised clearance simulated from the packaged model (lines, 200 subjects per PMA) with the maintainers' readings of the published simulated percentiles (points)."}
fig2_long <- fig2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "pct", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(value))
q_long <- q_var |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p05, p50, p95), names_to = "pct", values_to = "value")
ggplot2::ggplot(q_long, ggplot2::aes(PAGE, value, linetype = pct)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = fig2_long, ggplot2::aes(PAGE, value, shape = pct),
                      inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.5, colour = "firebrick") +
  ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = c(p05 = "dashed", p50 = "solid", p95 = "dashed")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)",
                y = "Allometrically normalised CL (L/h/70kg)",
                linetype = "Simulated", shape = "Figure 2") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

Table 2 also gives IIV only as CV%, and the paper does not say whether
CV% was computed as `sqrt(omega^2)` or `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`. The
packaged model uses `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The two readings differ
materially only for the Hill coefficient (102 CV%: 0.713 vs 1.040).
Re-solving with the alternative, on the same random-number stream,
shows how far the Figure 2 percentiles move:

```{r omega-scale}
cl_mod_om <- cl_mod |>
  rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ 0.113^2, etaltm50_cl ~ 0.174^2, etalhill ~ 1.02^2)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160801)
sim_om <- rxode2::rxSolve(cl_mod_om, vpc_data, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()
q_om <- pct(sim_om)
om_tab <- q_var |>
  dplyr::inner_join(q_om, by = "PAGE", suffix = c("_log", "_sq")) |>
  dplyr::filter(PAGE %in% fig2$PAGE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    PAGE,
    d05 = p05_sq - p05_log, d50 = p50_sq - p50_log, d95 = p95_sq - p95_log
  )
knitr::kable(
  om_tab |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "PMA (weeks)" = PAGE, "Change in 5th" = d05,
      "Change in 50th" = d50, "Change in 95th" = d95
    ),
  digits = 2
)
```

The shifts are small next to the uncertainty of reading percentiles off
the published figure, so Figure 2 cannot tell the two conventions
apart and the log-normal conversion is kept.

# Validation 3: metabolite / parent ratios (Figure 3)

Figure 3 plots the 25-OH / sirolimus and 16-O-DM / sirolimus ratios
against PMA with a simple Emax regression line and a 95% prediction
band; the paper prints only R^2 (0.34 and 0.30). The packaged Emax and
half-maximal PMA were obtained by digitising each regression line along
its whole length and fitting the Emax form to it; the line passes
through the origin, so there is no baseline term. The residual SD comes
from the prediction band at PMA 0, where the fitted line and its
standard error vanish and the band half-width is
`t(0.975, n - 2) * s`.

As an independent check, the maintainers also digitised the plotted
observations themselves and refitted the authors' stated method
(unweighted simple Emax by nonlinear least squares). The refit should
land near the packaged values and recover the printed R^2.

```{r ratio-refit}
pts_25oh <- data.frame(
  PAGE = c(55, 62, 63, 67, 67, 70, 71, 73, 74, 74, 76, 79, 81, 86, 95, 96, 96,
           109, 117, 126, 131, 161, 188, 188, 191, 191, 192, 236, 240),
  ratio = c(0.021, 0.044, 0.049, 0.045, 0.092, 0.060, 0.103, 0.070, 0.060,
            0.060, 0.045, 0.075, 0.104, 0.040, 0.083, 0.117, 0.112, 0.084,
            0.112, 0.106, 0.067, 0.084, 0.057, 0.054, 0.074, 0.140, 0.156,
            0.123, 0.155)
)
pts_16odm <- data.frame(
  PAGE = c(55, 63, 67, 66, 68, 72, 73, 74, 74, 75, 80, 82, 86, 95, 97, 97,
           109, 117, 126, 131, 161, 188, 188, 191, 192, 193, 236, 240),
  ratio = c(0.017, 0.021, 0.017, 0.054, 0.068, 0.071, 0.036, 0.034, 0.037,
            0.025, 0.088, 0.063, 0.028, 0.067, 0.075, 0.077, 0.042, 0.065,
            0.040, 0.040, 0.041, 0.028, 0.070, 0.083, 0.112, 0.095, 0.071,
            0.105)
)

refit <- function(d) {
  f <- stats::nls(ratio ~ emax * PAGE / (tm50 + PAGE), data = d,
                  start = list(emax = 0.2, tm50 = 100))
  ss <- sum(stats::residuals(f)^2)
  c(stats::coef(f),
    R2 = 1 - ss / sum((d$ratio - mean(d$ratio))^2),
    s = sqrt(ss / (nrow(d) - 2)))
}
packaged <- function(name) {
  ini <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(name))$iniDf
  th <- setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
  c(emax = exp(th[["lemax"]]), tm50 = exp(th[["ltm50"]]), s = th[["addSd"]])
}
r25 <- refit(pts_25oh); r16 <- refit(pts_16odm)
p25 <- packaged("Emoto_2016_sirolimus_25oh_ratio")
p16 <- packaged("Emoto_2016_sirolimus_16odm_ratio")

ratio_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Metabolite = rep(c("25-OH", "16-O-DM"), each = 4),
  Quantity = rep(c("Emax", "PMA at half-max (weeks)", "Residual SD", "R^2"), 2),
  Packaged = c(p25[["emax"]], p25[["tm50"]], p25[["s"]], NA,
               p16[["emax"]], p16[["tm50"]], p16[["s"]], NA),
  `Refit of digitised points` = c(r25[["emax"]], r25[["tm50"]], r25[["s"]], r25[["R2"]],
                                  r16[["emax"]], r16[["tm50"]], r16[["s"]], r16[["R2"]]),
  Published = c(NA, NA, NA, 0.34, NA, NA, NA, 0.30)
)
knitr::kable(ratio_tab, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(r25[["R2"]] - 0.34) < 0.05, abs(r16[["R2"]] - 0.30) < 0.05,
  abs(r25[["emax"]] / p25[["emax"]] - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(r25[["tm50"]] / p25[["tm50"]] - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(r16[["emax"]] / p16[["emax"]] - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(r16[["tm50"]] / p16[["tm50"]] - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(r25[["s"]] / p25[["s"]] - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(r16[["s"]] / p16[["s"]] - 1) < 0.15
)
```

```{r ratio-sim}
ratio_grid <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 250, by = 2), evid = 0L,
                         PAGE = seq(0, 250, by = 2))
sim25 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Emoto_2016_sirolimus_25oh_ratio")),
                         ratio_grid, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim16 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Emoto_2016_sirolimus_16odm_ratio")),
                         ratio_grid, keep = "PAGE") |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim25$mpr_25oh - p25[["emax"]] * sim25$PAGE / (p25[["tm50"]] + sim25$PAGE))) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(sim16$mpr_16odm - p16[["emax"]] * sim16$PAGE / (p16[["tm50"]] + sim16$PAGE))) < 1e-10
)
band <- function(sim, value, s, n) {
  data.frame(PAGE = sim$PAGE, fit = sim[[value]],
             lo = sim[[value]] - stats::qt(0.975, n - 2) * s,
             hi = sim[[value]] + stats::qt(0.975, n - 2) * s)
}
plot_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  band(sim25, "mpr_25oh", p25[["s"]], nrow(pts_25oh)) |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "A: 25-OH / sirolimus"),
  band(sim16, "mpr_16odm", p16[["s"]], nrow(pts_16odm)) |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "B: 16-O-DM / sirolimus")
)
pts_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pts_25oh |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "A: 25-OH / sirolimus"),
  pts_16odm |> dplyr::mutate(panel = "B: 16-O-DM / sirolimus")
)
```

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Emoto 2016: packaged simple Emax ratio models (solid) with an approximate 95% prediction band (dotted; residual SD only, ignoring parameter uncertainty) and the maintainers' digitisation of the plotted observations."}
ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(PAGE)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = fit), linewidth = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = lo), linetype = "dotted") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = hi), linetype = "dotted") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = pts_df, ggplot2::aes(PAGE, ratio), shape = 1) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)",
                y = "Metabolite / sirolimus concentration ratio") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Not a concentration model.** The packaged clearance model predicts
  a Bayesian clearance estimate, exactly as the authors fitted it; it
  cannot simulate concentrations on its own, because no volume or
  absorption rate is reported. Its observation `CL_wt70` and the ratio
  observations `mpr_25oh` / `mpr_16odm` are not registered output
  names, so `checkModelConventions()` reports one non-canonical-output
  warning per model. This follows the shipped clearance-maturation
  precedent `Kata_2025_ganciclovir_maturation` (`CL_bsa`).
* **Residual error scale.** Table 2 prints the proportional residual
  error as 0.066 without saying whether it is a variance or an SD.
  Taken as the NONMEM `$SIGMA` variance (`propSd = sqrt(0.066)`),
  because only that reading reproduces the Figure 2 prediction
  interval (Validation 2). The bootstrap median (0.067) is consistent
  with either reading.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 gives IIV as CV%. Converted with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The paper does not say which formula it
  used; the alternative `omega^2 = CV^2` matters only for the Hill
  coefficient (0.713 vs 1.040); the "omega-scale" comparison in
  Validation 2 shows the VPC cannot discriminate between them.
* **Weight exponent fixed at 0.67.** The authors estimated it in a
  separate regression on 3-19 year olds and applied it as a fixed
  normalisation before the NONMEM fit, so it is `fixed()` here. The
  Discussion also reports a sensitivity fit with exponent 0.75
  (CLmatured 20.6 L/h/70kg, TM50 60.1 weeks, Hill 2.84, "detailed data
  not shown"); with no IIV or residual values it is not packaged.
* **Covariate units.** `PAGE` is supplied in weeks (the paper's scale),
  not the register's default months; `WT` is used only to convert the
  normalised prediction to `CL_abs` in L/h.
* **Metabolite-ratio parameters are digitised.** Emax, half-maximal
  PMA and the residual SD of the two ratio models were read from
  Figure 3 by the maintainers (regression line and prediction band);
  the refit of the digitised observations reproduces the printed R^2.
  The ratio regressions had no random effects. The number of points
  (29 and 28) was counted from the figure and enters only the
  t-quantile used to convert the band to a residual SD.
* **Not packaged.** The Simcyp PBPK simulation of Supplemental Figure 3
  (TM50 61.3 weeks) is a platform-model output, not a model fitted in
  this paper, and the regression of clearance on body weight
  (Supplemental Figure 1A) survives only as the 0.67 exponent.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction for this article was found in
  PubMed (record and erratum search, checked 2026-11-24).
